title: Viral vector-mediated measurement of transcription factor activity in mouse brain
author: Yamamoto, Abe

steps.title: Replace TFBS in plasmids
steps.instruction: Synthesize the target TF binding sequence flanked by HindIII and BamHI sites, then subclone it between the HindIII and BamHI sites of plasmids pLV‑TFrep#1‑#6. Confirm that the new TFBS drives reporter expression using an in‑vitro luciferase assay before proceeding.

substeps.instruction: Subclone the TFBS into pLV‑TFrep#1‑#6 between HindIII and BamHI.

steps.title: Prepare transfection‑grade plasmid stock
steps.instruction: Dilute each plasmid to 1 µg/µL; 18 µg of each plasmid is required to transfect one 15 cm dish of HEK293T cells. Base plasmids #1‑#6 are available from Addgene (catalog numbers 182054‑182059). Store plasmid stocks at –80 °C.

steps.title: Transfect HEK293T cells with plasmids
steps.instruction: Perform PEI‑mediated transfection in one 15 cm dish of HEK293T cells using the following reagents and timing.

substeps.instruction: Mix 18 µg reporter construct with 20 µg third‑generation lentiviral packaging and envelope plasmids (pRSV‑Rev 5.3 µg, pMDLg/RRE 11 µg, pMD2.G 3.6 µg).
Dilute the plasmid mixture with 167 µL Opti‑MEM.
Add 300 µL PEI (prepared in 540 µL Opti‑MEM) to the diluted plasmids and mix.
Incubate the mixture for 20 min at room temperature.
Add the 1 mL transfection mixture to the cells.
After 16 h, replace medium with DMEM containing 10 % FBS and penicillin/streptomycin and continue culture.

steps.title: Harvest and filter virus‑containing medium
steps.instruction: 48 h after transfection, collect the culture medium and filter it through a 0.45 µm pore‑size filter.

steps.title: Precipitate virus with condensation solution
steps.instruction: Add 4 × Virus Condensation Solution to the filtered medium to achieve a final 1 × concentration, then store the mixture at 4 °C for 16 h.

steps.title: Centrifuge and resuspend virus pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the condensed virus at 4,350 × g, 4 °C, and dissolve the resulting pellet in 1 mL PBS.

steps.title: Purify virus via sucrose cushion
steps.instruction: Overlay the PBS‑resuspended virus onto a 20 % sucrose/PBS solution.

steps.title: Centrifuge and resuspend final virus pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the overlay at 15,000 × g, 4 °C, then dissolve the pellet in 50 µL PBS.

steps.title: Aliquot and store virus at –80 °C
steps.instruction: Divide the 50 µL virus solution into 4 µL aliquots and store them at –80 °C. Avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Determine virus titer by qPCR
steps.instruction: Transduce HEK293T cells with the virus aliquots and quantify integrated viral genomes by quantitative PCR. Ensure the preparation has a titer of at least 2.0 × 10¹⁰ infectious units per mL for in‑vivo TF activity measurements.

steps.title: Obtain pregnant E15 mouse
steps.instruction: Select a pregnant female mouse carrying E15 embryos. If purchased, acclimatize the dam in the animal facility for at least 3 days before surgery.

steps.title: Sterilize surgical instruments with ethanol
steps.instruction: Disinfect all surgical tools by immersing them in 70 % ethanol before the procedure.

steps.title: Warm PBS to 40‑42 °C
steps.instruction: Maintain approximately 10 mL of sterile PBS at 40 °C–42 °C using a heat‑block incubator.

steps.title: Fabricate glass injection needles
steps.instruction: Heat‑elongate a fine glass capillary with a micropipette puller set to 62 °C, then polish the tip to a 45° angle using a micropipette beveler.

steps.title: Prepare virus mixture for injection
steps.instruction: Mix each TF‑activity reporter virus with Cortex Buffer to obtain ~1 µL of virus mixture per embryo, then add Fast Green to a final concentration of 0.002 % (0.1 % stock) for visualisation.

substeps.instruction: Combine reporter viruses with Cortex Buffer (≈1 µL per embryo).
Add Fast Green to reach 0.002 % final concentration.

steps.title: Load needle and connect to pressure source
steps.instruction: Attach the polished glass needle to a syringe‑based needle holder (rubber gasket glued) and connect the holder to a pressure source. Use virus stocks with titers between 2.0 × 10¹⁰ and 8.0 × 10¹² IU/mL, preparing fresh aliquots (4 µL) immediately before injection.

description: The identity of cells is established by the joint activity of multiple TFs that are dynamically regulated by various stimuli (Takahashi and Yamanaka, 2006; Vaquerizas et al., 2009; Spitz and Furlong, 2012; Lambert et al., 2018). Thus, quantitative measurement of the activities of various TFs and how those activities change upon experimental stimulation will aid the trans-omics understanding of how cells respond to a variety of biological stimuli. However, it is still challenging to measure the endogenous activity of TF, particularly in vivo. Recently, we have reported the measurement of TF activity in vivo by using viral-vector-based TF activity reporters (Abe et al., 2015; Abe and Abe, 2022). This protocol describes the detailed procedures used in those studies for measuring the transcription factor activities of multiple TFs in the brain of mice.
